prompt:
Agents can't do anything with households yet: Spoonjoy's actions and MCP tools have nothing for them. Add the agent side. The households service already has createHousehold, listHouseholds, getHousehold, renameHousehold, createInvite, emailInvite, previewInvite, acceptInvite, revokeInvite, changeMemberRole, removeFromHousehold and leave (app/domains/households-and-identity). Plan the actions: their ids, inputs, outputs, consent, and the descriptions agents read.

Reply with your answer in this chat; don't change any files.

events.message: I'll check the service and the existing action declarations before planning.

arguments.command: cd app/domains/households-and-identity && ls -R . | head -50; ls ../../../actions; grep -rn "export async function\|export function" --include=*.ts . | grep -i "household\|invite\|member\|leave" | head -40
arguments.description: Inspect households domain and actions folder

arguments.command: cd actions && sed -n 1,80p shopping.mts; grep -n "consent\|Consent" *.mts | head -30
arguments.description: Read example action declaration and consent usage

arguments.command: cd app/domains/households-and-identity && sed -n 1,60p application/households.server.ts | head -80; sed -n 60,250p application/households.server.ts | grep -n "export\|Promise<\|role\|Result" | head -60; cat model/household.ts | sed -n 1,35p; sed -n 1,30p model/invite.ts; cd ../../../actions; sed -n 95,125p access.mts; ls ../app/domains/platform/flags/flags/; grep -n "consequential" ../tools/ouro-actions/ouro-actions.mts | head -5
arguments.description: Read service signatures, models, consent levels, flags

events.message:
I read the service, the household model and the existing `actions/*.mts` declarations. Nothing was changed. This is the plan.

## Shape
- Add `actions/households.mts` and add it to `spoonjoy.actions.mts`.
- Declare every action first. Each MCP operation in `spoonjoy-api.server.ts` spreads `declaredOperation("<id>")`.
- Ship behind the existing `households` flag in `app/domains/platform/flags/flags/households.ts`. The MCP tools should not list or serve households while the flag is off.
- Then run `pnpm actions:generate`, commit `actions/generated/`, and write unit tests for the operations.
- Skip `ownerEmail` on these. It exists for local servers with no signed-in person, and households need a real caller whose membership is checked. If MCP needs a user for local servers, reuse the existing pattern rather than adding a household-specific one.

## Actions
`householdId` is `field.string`, "from list_households". Ids use the verb_noun style of the existing ones (`add_shopping_list_item`).

| Service call | id | Inputs | Output | Consent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| listHouseholds | `list_households` | none | `[{id, name, role, memberCount}]` | read |
| getHousehold | `get_household` | `householdId` | id, name, `me`, members (`userId`, name, role), invites (owner only) | read |
| createHousehold | `create_household` | `name` (≤80 chars) | `{id, name}` | write |
| renameHousehold | `rename_household` | `householdId`, `name` | `{id, name}` | write, idempotent |
| createInvite | `create_household_invite` | `householdId`, `role` (`member` or `viewer`, default `member`), `uses` (1–50), `days` (1–30, default 14), optional `email` | invite id, role, uses left, expiry, and the link | consequential |
| emailInvite | `email_household_invite` | `householdId`, `email`, `role`, `days` | `{to}` | consequential |
| previewInvite | `preview_household_invite` | `token` | household name, role, status (`usable`, `expired`, `revoked`, `used`) | read |
| acceptInvite | `accept_household_invite` | `token` | `{householdId, joined}` | consequential |
| revokeInvite | `revoke_household_invite` | `householdId`, `inviteId` | none | write, destructive, idempotent |
| changeMemberRole | `change_household_member_role` | `householdId`, `userId`, `role` (`owner`, `member` or `viewer`) | none | consequential |
| removeFromHousehold | `remove_from_household` | `householdId`, `userId` | none | consequential |
| leave | `leave_household` | `householdId` | none | consequential |

## Consent reasoning
- **Reads** are `list_households`, `get_household` and `preview_invite`.
- **Writes** act only on the person's own things: creating, renaming and revoking an invite.
- **Consequential** covers anything that reaches other people, changes who sees the household's shared lists, plan and recipes, or can't be undone:
  - Inviting by link or by email, and accepting an invite.
  - Changing a role, removing a member, and leaving.
  - The agent prepares these and the person approves.
- `revoke_household_invite` is destructive but only withdraws access, so it is write plus destructive.

## Descriptions
Two things need care.
- **Invite tokens.** `create_household_invite` returns the link once, because only its hash is stored. The agent description must say: "The link is shown only once. Give it to the person to pass on; don't post or log it." `get_household` never returns tokens, only invite metadata. The tool result should state what it did, for example "Invite created for role member, 1 use, expires <date>".
- **Role rules.** Put the service's refusals in the agent text so agents don't discover them by failing:
  - Only owners invite, rename, change roles or remove people.
  - Invites can't grant owner; promote after the person joins.
  - Nobody changes their own role.
  - A household keeps at least one owner.
  - An owner can't remove another owner until demoted.
  - A viewer is read-only.

Draft agent text for `change_household_member_role`: "Owner only. Set one member's role to owner, member or viewer. You can't change your own role, and the household must keep an owner."

## Errors
Map `Validated` failures to typed refusals:
- `forbidden` becomes a not-allowed refusal.
- `unavailable` becomes a retryable error. This is the email send path, so `email_household_invite` should say mail may be unavailable and to fall back to `create_household_invite`.
- Anything else becomes invalid input.

An unknown household or non-member gets the same not-found as `getHousehold` returning null, so existence isn't leaked.

## Restraint check (the bar)
- **Jobs.** The jobs are: see my households, set one up, bring someone in, change who can do what, and get out or remove someone.
- **Candidate to cut.** `preview_household_invite` is the one I'd cut if it breaks nothing. It exists so an agent can show what a link is before the person accepts, and `accept_household_invite` already returns a typed refusal for a bad token. I'd keep it, because accepting is consequential and the person should see the household and role first.
- **Merge decision.** Link and email invites could share one action. They use the same service function family but have different side effects: email sends mail and returns no link. I'd keep two ids for clarity, and the email one is cheaper to approve.

## Validation
- Unit tests:
  - A declared-actions test shows MCP tools equal the declarations.
  - One case per role-rule refusal.
  - Flag off means no tools listed.
  - The invite link is returned once and never appears in `get_household`.
- Also run `pnpm actions:check`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm run claims:check` if docs change.
- Journeys: add a journey only if a person-facing UI changes. Agent-door tests run in the unit and Workers lanes.
- Update `docs/claude-connector.md` and `docs/api.md` with the new tools.

criteria.evidence: The plan is built from the service list. The main table's first column is 'Service call', with one row per function. Jobs only show up at the end, in 'Restraint check': 'The jobs are: see my households, set one up, bring someone in...', after the actions were already chosen.

All 12 service functions become 12 actions. The answer weighs the obvious merge and rejects it ('I'd keep two ids for clarity'). It considers cutting preview_household_invite but keeps it. Nothing is merged or left out.

Some parts are good, such as 'Map `Validated` failures to typed refusals' and the not-found that doesn't leak existence. But the inputs aren't minimal. create_household_invite takes `uses`, `days` and an optional `email`, while email_household_invite separately takes `email`, `role` and `days`. Several outputs are 'none'. The consent choices are also questionable: accepting an invite and leaving a household affect only the person, yet both are 'consequential'. Most failure messages don't say what to do next. The one exception is the email fallback.

The Validation section lists only unit tests, `pnpm actions:check`, typecheck, lint and claims:check. It says 'add a journey only if a person-facing UI changes'. There is no plan for fresh agents to do a household job through the actions.

verdict.summary: The answer maps each service function to its own action. It neither starts from agent jobs nor merges or cuts actions, its inputs and consent are only partly well judged, and it plans no fresh-agent proof.
